grid.gaps_between_cells: none — cells touch edge to edge

alignment_guides.instruction: The uploaded reference image shows the grid. Black lines (#000000) are cell boundaries. Magenta lines (#FF00FF) are character alignment guides — the character's head must touch the magenta head-line and feet must touch the magenta feet-line in each row. AFTER drawing all characters, DELETE every #FF00FF magenta pixel. Keep characters INSIDE the black #000000 grid cells.

grid_dividers.positions: horizontal at y=256, y=512, y=768 and vertical at x=256, x=512, x=768
grid_dividers.purpose: cell boundaries — no character part may cross these

character_guides.purpose: character height alignment — top of mass touches top guide, base touches bottom guide
character_guides.removal: delete all #FF00FF magenta pixels from the final image

rows.facing: front-facing — creature faces straight toward the viewer
rows.what_viewer_sees: the front of the monster — multiple heads facing viewer, front of body mass
rows.column_1: idle frame 1 — menacing still pose, heads slightly raised
rows.column_2: idle frame 2 — one head weaves left, others shift
rows.column_3: idle frame 3 — heads recoil, body mass pulses
rows.column_4: idle frame 4 — return toward frame 1 pose

rows.facing: back-facing — creature faces away from viewer, showing its back
rows.what_viewer_sees: the back of the monster — rear of body mass, backs of heads

rows.facing: profile-left — creature faces toward 9 o'clock (left edge of image), viewer sees its RIGHT side
rows.what_viewer_sees: the right side profile of the monster

rows.facing: profile-right — creature faces toward 3 o'clock (right edge of image), viewer sees its LEFT side
rows.what_viewer_sees: the left side profile of the monster

subject.name: Scylla (Monster Form)
subject.description: tragic sea monster from Greek mythology — once a beautiful woman, now a horrific multi-headed creature. Monstrous and dangerous but clearly tragic rather than generic evil.
subject.form: broad distorted upper mass with multiple head suggestion (simplify to 2-3 readable grouped head forms), unstable asymmetry acceptable, sea-monster anatomy with human-remnant cues

palette.accents: bruised purple or cold cyan highlights

subject.expression: suffering/rage hybrid — this creature is in pain, not just angry

style.aesthetic: pixelated retro style, high quality and modern like Stardew Valley — clean readable sprites with flat shading
style.outline: dark 1-pixel outline around the entire creature
style.shading: flat cluster shading, no smooth gradients
style.antialiasing: none — crisp pixel edges only, no blur
style.character_height: 70% of cell height (approximately 180 pixels in each 256-pixel cell)
style.character_centering: horizontally centered in each cell, top of mass touching top guide, base touching bottom guide

rules: this is ONE image containing 16 small creatures in a grid — NOT 16 separate images
every creature in all 16 cells is the SAME monster with the SAME form, proportions, and colors
this is a MONSTER — not a human. Scylla is a multi-headed sea creature, not a person
maintain the same monster mass and silhouette across all directions — side views should not collapse into a generic blob
no creature may cross a cell boundary into a neighboring cell
all tops within a row must align on the row's top guide line
all bases within a row must align on the row's bottom guide line
identical top-left lighting across all 16 cells
no tilt or rotation on any creature
